mission:
Add a text utility module to this library as ONE task (do not split it into several tasks): src/text.js with node:test tests in test/text.test.js.
It exports four functions, each with its own tests. In wrap, truncate and countWords a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters.
1. `slugify(text)`: lower-case, strip diacritics (NFD), replace every run of characters other than a-z and 0-9 with a single "-", trim "-" from both ends; throws TypeError when the argument is not a string.
2. `wrap(text, width)`: greedy word wrap into lines of at most `width` characters, a word longer than the width alone on its line; returns the lines joined with a line feed; throws TypeError unless width is a positive integer.
3. `truncate(text, max)`: returns the text unchanged when it fits; otherwise the longest prefix of whole words that fits in `max - 1` characters followed by "…" (when not even the first word fits: its first `max - 1` characters followed by "…").
4. `countWords(text)`: the number of words; 0 for an empty or all-whitespace string.
Record one design decision with the decision tool stating that word definition. `npm test` must pass. Commit as you see fit.

plan.summary: Add a new ESM module src/text.js exporting slugify, wrap, truncate and countWords, with node:test tests in test/text.test.js, as a single worker task (as requested). The repo is a tiny dependency-free ESM package (package.json has "type": "module" and "test": "node --test"; the existing test/index.test.js uses node:test with node:assert/strict, semicolon-free, single quotes), so the new files follow that style and are picked up by `npm test` automatically. The same task records the word-definition design decision and commits the work.
assumptions: Lengths are measured in JavaScript string length (UTF-16 code units); "fits" in truncate means text.length <= max.
Whitespace means what the regex class \s matches; a word is a maximal run of \S characters.
wrap rebuilds lines from the words joined by single spaces (original whitespace runs, including existing line breaks, are not preserved); empty or all-whitespace input yields an empty string.

truncate's "longest prefix of whole words" is a prefix of the original text cut at the end of a word (original inner whitespace kept, no trailing whitespace before the "…"); the request does not settle this versus re-joining words with single spaces.
truncate's first-word fallback applies to text that starts with a word; behaviour for leading whitespace and for invalid max values is unspecified by the request and is not given extra validation.

slugify strips diacritics by NFD-normalising and removing combining marks (U+0300–U+036F) before the non-alphanumeric replacement; characters with no a-z/0-9 decomposition (e.g. "ß", "ø") become separators.
Only slugify (non-string argument) and wrap (width not a positive integer) are required to throw TypeError; no extra argument validation is added to the other functions.
src/index.js is not changed (no re-export was requested); the functions are imported directly from src/text.js.
The design decision is recorded by the worker during the task (not by the planner) so exactly one decision is recorded.

tasks.title: Add src/text.js (slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords) with node:test tests
tasks.description:
Repository: a tiny dependency-free ESM package "textkit" (package.json: "type": "module", scripts.test = "node --test"; Node v24 is installed; native Windows, no POSIX tools assumed). Existing files: src/index.js (only `export const VERSION = '1.0.0'`) and test/index.test.js (imports `test` from 'node:test' and `assert` from 'node:assert/strict', no semicolons, single quotes). Match that style. Do not modify src/index.js, package.json, README.md or the existing test, and add no dependencies.

Create src/text.js with four named exports. In wrap, truncate and countWords a WORD is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters (regex \S+); lengths are string .length.

1. slugify(text): throw TypeError if typeof text is not 'string'. Otherwise lower-case, normalise with NFD and remove combining diacritical marks (U+0300–U+036F), replace every run of characters other than a-z and 0-9 with a single "-", and trim "-" from both ends. Example: 'Crème Brûlée!' -> 'creme-brulee'; '  Hello,  World  ' -> 'hello-world'; '' or '!!!' -> ''.

2. wrap(text, width): throw TypeError unless width is a positive integer (Number.isInteger(width) && width > 0; so 0, -1, 1.5, NaN, '10', undefined all throw). Greedy word wrap: put words on the current line separated by a single space while the line stays at most `width` characters, otherwise start a new line; a word longer than width sits alone on its own line (it is not split). Return the lines joined with a line feed ("\n"). Empty or all-whitespace text returns ''. Example: wrap('the quick brown fox', 10) -> 'the quick\nbrown fox'; wrap('a extraordinarily b', 5) -> 'a\nextraordinarily\nb'.

3. truncate(text, max): if text.length <= max return text unchanged. Otherwise return the longest prefix of whole words that fits in max - 1 characters, followed by the single character "…" (U+2026) — the prefix is taken from the original text and ends at the end of a word, with no trailing whitespace before the ellipsis. When not even the first word fits in max - 1 characters, return the first max - 1 characters of that word followed by "…". The result therefore never exceeds max characters. Examples: truncate('hello world', 11) -> 'hello world'; truncate('hello brave world', 12) -> 'hello brave…'; truncate('hello world', 8) -> 'hello…'; truncate('extraordinary', 5) -> 'extr…'.

4. countWords(text): the number of words; 0 for '' and for an all-whitespace string. Example: countWords('  one\ttwo\n three ') -> 3.

Create test/text.test.js using node:test and node:assert/strict, importing from '../src/text.js', with separate tests for each of the four functions covering the normal cases and the edge cases above (slugify: diacritics, punctuation/whitespace runs collapsing to one '-', trimming, TypeError for non-strings such as 42, null, undefined; wrap: greedy packing, exact-fit line, over-long word alone on its line, multiple whitespace/tabs/newlines between words, empty input, TypeError for invalid widths; truncate: fits/exact fit unchanged, whole-word cut, cut that lands exactly on a word end, first word too long, result length <= max; countWords: empty, all-whitespace, mixed whitespace, single word). Tests must assert real behaviour — do not hard-code implementation to tests or weaken assertions.

Record exactly ONE design decision with the decision tool (mcp__nexus__record_decision) stating the word definition: in wrap, truncate and countWords a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters, with a brief rationale (one consistent definition across the three functions, per the request).

Run `npm test` and make sure it passes (existing version test plus the new tests). Then commit only src/text.js and test/text.test.js on the current branch with a concise message, ending the commit message with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Leave no temporary files behind.
acceptanceCriteria: src/text.js exports named functions slugify, wrap, truncate and countWords and nothing else is modified outside src/text.js and test/text.test.js (verify with `git show --stat HEAD` / `git status`).
slugify('Crème Brûlée!') returns 'creme-brulee', slugify('  Hello,  World  ') returns 'hello-world', and slugify(42) throws TypeError.

wrap('the quick brown fox', 10) returns 'the quick\nbrown fox'; a word longer than the width appears alone on its line unsplit; wrap('a b', 0), wrap('a b', 1.5) and wrap('a b', '5') each throw TypeError.
truncate('hello world', 11) returns 'hello world'; truncate('hello brave world', 12) returns 'hello brave…'; truncate('hello world', 8) returns 'hello…'; truncate('extraordinary', 5) returns 'extr…'.
countWords('') and countWords('   \n\t ') return 0; countWords('  one\ttwo\n three ') returns 3.
test/text.test.js uses node:test and has at least one test for each of the four functions, including the TypeError cases for slugify and wrap.
`npm test` exits 0 with all tests (existing and new) passing and none skipped.
Exactly one decision is recorded via mcp__nexus__record_decision stating that a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters in wrap, truncate and countWords.
The work is committed and `git status` reports a clean working tree.

risks.description: The truncate wording is ambiguous for multi-space or leading-whitespace input (prefix of the original text versus words re-joined with single spaces).
risks.mitigation: The task fixes one interpretation (prefix of the original text cut at a word end, no trailing whitespace before the ellipsis) and states it as an assumption; tests concentrate on the cases the request specifies unambiguously.

risks.description: Off-by-one errors in truncate (max - 1 budget plus the ellipsis) or in wrap's exact-fit line handling.
risks.mitigation: Acceptance criteria include concrete exact-fit and boundary examples, and tests assert the result length never exceeds max.

risks.description: The "…" character or accented test strings could be corrupted by a non-UTF-8 file encoding on Windows.
risks.mitigation: Write both files as UTF-8 (or use the … escape in source); the truncate and slugify tests would fail visibly under `npm test` if the encoding were wrong.

risks.description: The decision could be recorded more than once (e.g. on a task retry), violating the "one design decision" requirement.
risks.mitigation: Only the single worker task records it, and the task description states exactly one; on a retry the worker should not record it again if it was already recorded.
